open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 orphan value-byte cleanup
open_points.text: On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... are removed; nothing else is.
open_points.question: What happens when an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be removed or cleanup is interrupted: does the kernel refuse to start, proceed while never serving it, or take another action?
options: Proceed and leave it unserved until a later start
Proceed but retry cleanup during this start
open_points.default_guess: Proceed, never serve the file, and retry removal at a later start, matching the stated treatment of an unremovable obsolete spool directory.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 record reachability
open_points.question: Exactly which records count as naming value bytes: any StoredValue record carrying the digest, only records that refer to a StoredValue by value_id, or transitive reachability from retained domain and trace records?
options: Any StoredValue record with that value_digest
Any record directly or indirectly referring to the StoredValue
Only retained root records such as traces, runs, cases and flow versions
open_points.default_guess: Treat any persisted StoredValue record carrying the digest as naming the bytes.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 startup sequence
open_points.text: On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... are removed
open_points.question: At what point relative to A14 recovery and advancement are unreferenced value bytes removed, and may recovery publish or reuse value bytes before this cleanup completes?
open_points.default_guess: After opening and validating the store, remove unreferenced bytes before A14 recovery begins, then allow recovery to republish any bytes it derives.
